body.html: Who The Green Residence 304 is for — let me put it the way I'd tell a friend first: this isn't a hillside resort that takes you stargazing and rafting, the kind of thing many people picture when they hear the word Prachinburi · The Green Residence 304 is an aparthotel and residence for people who actually have business in the 304 Industrial Park area, in Tha Tum subdistrict, Si Maha Phot district · the people it suits best, and who'll probably get the most out of it, are those working in the park — engineers, staff posted here for weeks or months, suppliers who come in to inspect work for a while, and families visiting someone who works in the park · because the place was conceived as a residence from the start, you can stay either by the day for just a few nights, or by the month if you need to settle in for the long haul — a flexibility ordinary hotels rarely offer · another group it fits well is budget travellers driving the 304 route (Kabin Buri–Chachoengsao) who want to stop for a night somewhere clean, good-looking and not pricey · for anyone chasing a full holiday atmosphere — forests, waterfalls, big swimming pools or lively nightlife — I'll be straight with you, this may not be the answer, because it's an industrial-park stay built around making daily life and work convenient rather than around entertainment · put simply, if you come expecting "a good-looking, good-value place near work," there's a good chance you'll be happy here, but if you come with a dream resort in mind, you'll need to adjust your expectations a little.

Location and getting around — the selling point of The Green Residence 304 is the location, plain and simple · the place sits at 201 Moo 4, Bu Yai Bai Road, Tha Tum subdistrict, Si Maha Phot district, in the 304 Industrial Park area, one of the larger industrial parks in the east · the clearest advantage is that it's just about 5 minutes' drive from the 304 Industrial Park, and around 15 minutes from the Rojana Prachinburi park, so workers don't have to wake up that early to fight traffic to clock in · food and daily essentials are no worry either, because Big C and Major Cineplex Si Maha Phot are about 2.3 kilometres away, a few minutes' drive, with a supermarket, restaurants and a cinema to unwind at after work · closer still there's a 7-Eleven about 1.5 km away and a Lotus's about 2.5 km · on the health side there's Chularat 304 Hospital about 2.4 km away, reassuring for anyone here long-term · if you want to make merit or take a stroll, Wat Bu Yai Bai is just about 0.73 km away, while Wat Si Pho Malai is about 2.6 km · further afield: getting into Prachinburi town and the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Museum of Thai Traditional Medicine takes about 30–40 minutes' drive depending on the route, and if you want to carry on to Kabin Buri or the Khao Yai side of Prachin you can keep driving · one honest note: because it's in an industrial-park area, almost all travel here needs a car — it isn't a neighbourhood you can walk around — so without your own car or a motorbike, plan your transport ahead.

"I came to work in the park for several weeks, so I chose a monthly stay here. The rooms are done in wood tones and feel warmer than the usual dorms near the factories, there's a balcony to sit out on in the evening, it's quiet and I sleep well — the price is really good value for this area."

Room types and decor — The Green Residence 304 has around 30 rooms in total, conceived as a residence from the start, and what sets it apart from the usual industrial-park stays is the design · the building is a 5-storey block in contemporary Thai style, built mainly around wood — both the interior woodwork and the choice of warm brown tones from the timber — giving a natural feel rather than the stiff look of an ordinary shophouse rental · the rooms come in two main types · the first is the Green Deluxe at 36 sqm, of which there are about 10, the larger room, good for anyone who wants space to sit or work in the room · the second is the Green Superior at 30 sqm, of which there are about 20, the standard room, compact but still roomier than many rentals at a similar price · every room comes with a private balcony, a detail a lot of people like, because you can step out for some air or sit out in the evening once it cools down · inside, the rooms have air-conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a water heater, an en-suite bathroom with soap and shampoo, and what many reviews mention — a hotel-grade spring mattress that makes for a better night's sleep than the usual dorm bed · the decor is simple and clean, in warm wood tones, with nice photo spots along the corridors and common areas · for workers who need to take online meetings, the rooms have free Wi-Fi — I'd suggest testing the signal strength in the actual room when you check in, because in a place this size the signal can vary a bit depending on the room's position.

Facilities and common areas — you have to understand first that The Green Residence 304 is a compact, residence-style stay, not a full resort hotel, so the facilities focus on day-to-day necessities rather than entertainment · the things it does have, and that genuinely make life easier, are a lift (important for a 5-storey building and for anyone dragging luggage or heavy bags), free parking for both cars and motorbikes, free Wi-Fi throughout the building, and a key-card building entry, CCTV and security system, which helps anyone staying alone or long-term feel safe · there's laundry and room-cleaning service, handy for workers who don't want to lose time on chores · the standout for atmosphere is the greenery and trees surrounding the building, true to the "Green" name, which keeps the evenings cooler and shadier than a bare rental block · what I'll say plainly so you don't expect the wrong thing is that there's no swimming pool and no in-house gym, and according to the latest information breakfast is still not included in the room rate · anyone who cares about a pool or gym may need to consider other options in areas that have them, but if your brief is a clean, safe room near work at good value, what's on offer here covers real living just fine.

Food and places around — on the food side, I'll be honest: The Green Residence 304 does not include breakfast and isn't a hotel with a big in-house dining room like a resort · but that's not a problem for a location like this, because the area around Si Maha Phot has a fair scatter of made-to-order eateries, curry-and-rice shops, coffee shops and convenience stores, especially along the main roads and near the park entrance · the key thing is that Big C and Lotus's, about 2.3–2.5 kilometres away, have both supermarkets and food courts, so you can easily buy food and supplies to stock in your room · for anyone on a monthly or long stay, having a fridge in every room helps you keep food and drinking water, and the 7-Eleven about 1.5 km away helps with quick late-night bites · put simply, you don't come here to eat at the property — you use it as a base and head out for food nearby, of which there's enough to live on · anyone who likes to cook should ask the property clearly about using electrical appliances in the room first, because residence-style places each have different rules, and the room details listed for online booking mostly note basic equipment like a fridge and water heater.

Service — service at a small place like this usually comes down to the owner and the team looking after it directly, which is both an upside and something to understand · the upside is that when a place isn't large, getting in touch, reporting a problem or asking for help is usually direct and quick, without going through several departments like a big chain hotel · the few voices in online reviews rate the service well and mention how quiet and orderly the place is · because it takes both daily and monthly guests, the team is used to looking after long-stayers — things like renewing contracts, paying for water and electricity, and reporting repairs · what to keep in mind, as is natural with a small place, is that there may not be staff at the counter around the clock like a big hotel, so if you arrive late or have a special request, let the property know and arrange a time clearly in advance · overall, the service here leans on being friendly and hands-on rather than the formality of an international-grade hotel, which fits the kind of guests who mostly come to work and stay.

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — to be transparent, I have to say that The Green Residence 304 has only recently opened for booking on online platforms, so it still has only a small number of reviews compared with hotels that have been open a long time, so the picture below is pulled together from what reviews there are on Trip.com and Agoda, mixed with information from accommodation guides and rental listings in the area · on the praise side: the points people agree on are the location close to the 304 Industrial Park, making the commute to work easy; the quiet, natural atmosphere with trees around and cool evenings; the warm wood-toned design that photographs well; clean rooms and comfortable spring mattresses; and the good value for both daily and monthly stays · on the watch-out side: the main thing is that it's a quiet industrial-park stay with few attractions or activities around, so it suits people coming to work more than to holiday; the property has no swimming pool and doesn't include breakfast; and because it's a small place that's still new on the booking system, review information is still thin, so you should ask the property directly about room details, equipment and service before booking for clarity · in short, anyone who comes understanding that this is a good-looking residence in an industrial-park area is usually happy, while anyone hoping for resort-style facilities may feel something's still missing.

"The room is clean, the wood tones look good, it's quiet and secure with a key card and CCTV · the only catch is that it's surrounded by an industrial-park area with not many places to visit. If you're here to work it's a great fit, but if you want to sightsee you have to drive out a fair way."

Price and value — daily rates at The Green Residence 304 start at around THB 600/night (on some platforms and at some times it runs around THB 682, or an average of around THB 891 depending on the room type and dates), which puts it in the budget bracket for a room that looks this good · for anyone who needs to settle in for a month, the property has monthly rates in the range of around THB 3,500–7,500 per month depending on the room type and conditions (water and electricity are generally billed separately by actual usage — ask the property), which brings the cost per night down a lot compared with paying daily · compared with other stays in the 304 Industrial Park area — both dorms and apartments near the factories that are just for sleeping, and higher-tier hotels like The Canal 304 or Kantary 304 that have a pool and fuller facilities but cost more — The Green Residence 304 positions itself in the good-looking, budget stay bracket, where the selling points are the wood-toned design, the private balcony, cleanliness and security, on an affordable budget · for a company posting several staff here, or for anyone settling in long-term themselves, choosing the monthly rate here is good value, because you get a more comfortable room than the usual dorm at not much extra cost · but if your brief calls for a swimming pool, gym and in-house breakfast, the value shifts to the higher-priced options instead.

Good to know before booking — there are several things that help a stay go more smoothly · one, decide first whether you're staying daily or monthly, because if you'll be here longer than two weeks, asking about the monthly rate is usually far better value than booking by the night through a platform, and you should ask clearly how water and electricity are billed separately · two, the property doesn't include breakfast and has no swimming pool — if those two things matter to you, set your expectations in advance, or use Big C and the shops nearby to help with food · three, because it's an industrial-park area where almost everything needs a car, if you're not driving in yourself, prepare a transport plan or rent a motorbike beforehand · four, the property is small and still new on the online booking system, so you should contact it directly to confirm room availability, in-room equipment and check-in time, especially if you'll arrive late · five, standard check-in starts at 2:00 PM and check-out is before 12:00 PM, and the property does not allow pets · six, if you book through a platform, compare Trip.com against Agoda and pick a free-cancellation option to be safe if your plans aren't firm yet, because business plans often change.

The verdict — from the information and reviews available, The Green Residence 304 is the best fit for people who genuinely have business in the 304 Industrial Park area of Si Maha Phot and want a good-looking, clean, safe room at a budget price, available both daily and monthly · what makes it more interesting than the usual dorms near the factories is the contemporary Thai design built around warm wood, a private balcony in every room, a hotel-grade spring mattress, trees all around, plus security like key cards and CCTV, and a location just about 5 minutes from the park · if you're looking for a full holiday atmosphere, a swimming pool, a gym or in-house breakfast, this may not be the answer, and you should consider The Canal 304 or the resorts on the Khao Yai and Noen Hom side instead · but for coming to work, being posted here, visiting someone in the park, or stopping over on the 304 route on a budget and easy on the eye — The Green Residence 304 is a fitting choice for that kind of stay in this area · I'd suggest contacting the property directly to confirm the details and latest prices before deciding, because it's still new on the booking system and some information may change.
